nodes.name: Ni foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: To remove the surface oxidized layer, a piece of Ni foam (2 cm × 3 cm) was cleaned through sonication consecutively in 3 M HCl, ethanol, and DI water (5 min each) prior to using as a substrate.
nodes.source_text: To remove the surface oxidized layer, a piece of Ni foam (2 cm × 3 cm) was cleaned through sonication consecutively in 3 M HCl, ethanol, and DI water (5 min each) prior to using as a substrate.

nodes.name: Ni-Co-carbonate hydroxide growth
nodes.procedure: A solution of 0.004 M nickel nitrate and 0.008 M cobalt nitrate was prepared in DI water (30 mL) with stirring. 0.012 M Urea was added to this solution as a reducing agent with stirring and then the mixture was stirred for 15 min to obtain a clear solution. This mixed solution was transferred into Teflon-lined stainless-steel 50 mL autoclave. For in situ growth of the catalyst, the surface-cleaned Ni foam was immersed into the solution. The autoclave was locked tightly and maintained at 120°C for 6 h in an electric oven. After the reaction, the uniformly grown Ni-Co-carbonates hydroxide nanowire arrays on Ni foam were removed from the solution and washed several times with DI water.

nodes.name: NiCo₂S₄ nanowire formation
nodes.procedure: Sodium sulfide flakes were used to prepare a 0.2 M solution in DI water (30 mL) while stirring for 10 min. This sulfide precursor solution was transferred to the same autoclave, containing the Ni-Co-carbonates hydroxide nanowire arrays grown on Ni foam, and maintained at 160°C for 8 h in an electric oven. After cooling to room temperature, the NiCo₂S₄ nanowire arrays grown on the Ni foam (NiCo₂S₄ NW/NF) were washed several times with ethanol and DI water, followed by drying at 60°C overnight in the vacuum oven.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCo₂S₄ NW/NF shows cubic phase (JCPDS: 98-062-4474) with characteristic peaks matching pure NiCo₂S₄ plus Ni foam peaks at 44.2° and 52°, and minor Ni₃S₂ impurity peak at 21.7°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffraction patterns for NiCo₂S₄ NW/NF (Figure 2c) are similar to that of NiCo₂S₄ (Figure 2b) with two strong characteristic peaks at 44.2° and 52° arising from the Ni foam (JCPDS: 98-004-3397). The peak at 21.7° (marked with an asterisk) is due to the small amount of Ni₃S₂ formed during the second step.

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM shows NiCo₂S₄ NW/NF forms uniform 3D hierarchical porous nanowire arrays covering entire Ni foam with sharp tips, mean diameter ≈70 nm, mean length ≈1 μm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3e reveals that the whole Ni foam substrate was covered closely and uniformly by the NiCo₂S₄ catalyst, forming a 3D hierarchical porous structure (Figure 3f).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of NiCo₂S₄ NW/NF shows polycrystalline nature with lattice spacings 0.28 nm (113 plane) and 0.16 nm (044 plane); SAED confirms polycrystalline structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of the nanowire arrays in Figure 4d reveals that the lattice planes had random orientations, consistent with the polycrystalline nature of the sample. The measured lattice spacings between two fringes in Figure 4d were 0.28 and 0.16 nm; we attribute them to the diffraction of the (113) and (044) lattice planes, respectively, of the NiCo₂S₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows uniform spatial distribution of Ni, Co, and S atoms over NiCo₂S₄ NW/NF nanowire arrays.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning TEM and EDX elemental mapping (Figure 4e-h) revealed the superposition of the uniform spatial distribution of Ni, Co, and S atoms over the examined detection range at the surface of the NiCo₂S₄ nanowire arrays.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of NiCo₂S₄ NW/NF shows Co 2p peaks at 778.8/793.7 eV (Co³⁺) and 781.6/797.3 eV (Co²⁺); Ni 2p peaks at 853.2/872.6 eV (Ni²⁺) and 856.2/874.4 eV (Ni³⁺); S 2p peaks at 161.8/163.1 eV (S 2p₁/₂/₃/₂) with M-S bond at 163.8 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We used XPS to characterize the chemical valence states of the various elements in the NiCo₂S₄ NW/NF structure... Thus, the XPS analysis confirmed that, near its surface, the sample had a composition of Co²⁺, Co³⁺, Ni²⁺, and Ni³⁺ cations, M-S bonds, and S²⁻ anions.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at scan rates 10-70 mV s⁻¹ gives Cdl = 40 mF cm⁻² for NiCo₂S₄ NW/NF (vs 6.9, 19.4, 2.6 mF cm⁻² for Ni₃S₂/NF, NiCo₂O₄/NF, bare NF), indicating highest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the CV curves, we measured the values of i_a and i_c at a potential of 0.875 V versus RHE... From these linear plots, we calculated values for the capacitances of NiCo₂S₄ NW/NF, Ni₃S₂/NF, NiCo₂O₄/NF, and the bare Ni foam of 40, 6.9, 19.4, and 2.6 mF cm⁻², respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS at 0.5 V shows NiCo₂S₄ NW/NF charge transfer resistance Rct ≈18 Ω (vs 24 Ω Ni₃S₂/NF, 58 Ω NiCo₂O₄/NF, 142 Ω bare NF), indicating fastest OER kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The hierarchical NiCo₂S₄ NW/NF displayed a charge transfer resistance of ≈18 Ω; the value for the Ni₃S₂/NF was slightly higher (24 Ω), but still low. The NiCo₂O₄/NF had an intermediate-value charge transfer resistance of 58 Ω, while the bare Ni foam possessed a very high charge transfer resistance of 142 Ω in the electrolyte.

nodes.characterization_summary: Static contact angle measurement shows NiCo₂S₄ NW/NF is highly hydrophilic with ≈15° (vs ≈110° for bare Ni foam), due to high surface roughness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast, the average contact angle of the NiCo₂S₄ NW/NF was ≈15° (Figure S4b, Supporting Information), suggesting an extremely hydrophilic surface.
